title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Zephyr Labs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Riley Gomez (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (Zephyr CTO), Jordan Lee (Eng Manager), Priya Rao (Security), Tom Evans (ML Eng)

[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. this is Alex from Redwood -- i'm the AE on the account, with Samir on the line who is our SE, and Riley from CSM. how's everybody doing?
[00:00:08] Maya: good thanks, hey all. busy week but excited to chat about quickstart.
[00:00:12] Jordan: yep, hi. we want to understand how fast we can get first token and then how we scale to more throughput.
[00:00:18] Alex: great, totally. high level agenda: quick intro, your stack and constraints, demo/quickstart experience and time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security checklist, and next steps. is that ok?
[00:00:30] Priya: yes, also want to cover audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:00:34] Samir: perfect, i'll dive into some latency and batching details when we get to tradeoffs.

[00:01:00] Alex: Maya, can you give a quick picture of your current infra and what you're evaluating?
[00:01:05] Maya: sure. Zephyr builds summarization and search features over internal docs and customer support tickets. we have a small infra team, self-hosted vector db (milvus) and some kubernetes clusters. right now we use a mix of OpenAI for some features and an internal smaller model for lower cost stuff. goal is to reduce cost and improve p99 latency for queries. also the security team needs to approve anything that touches customer PII.
[00:01:32] Tom: technical detail, our average request size is 600 tokens for context, with 128 tokens response target. p50 is fine but we care about p95/p99 under 600ms ideally.
[00:01:45] Jordan: timeline, we want to run a short pilot next month and decide by end of quarter.

[00:02:10] Alex: good context. short answer on quickstart: we have a PLG flow with free credits, API keys, and SDKs; time-to-first-token for a basic test is usually under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart, under 5 if you use our sample repo. we'll send you a quickstart link and a sandbox key so you can hit hosted inference quickly.
[00:02:28] Maya: that sounds promising. when you say hosted, is data persisted? we need to know retention and whether KV cache or logs persist customer content.
[00:02:36] Riley: we default to short retention for hosted sandbox, and logs for debugging are available to the customer; by default hosted API does not retain customer prompts beyond 30 days unless configured. for enterprise contracts we offer different retention windows and optional private deployments where data never leaves the VPC.
[00:02:55] Priya: ok we will need SOC2 + KMS details. is SSO available for the console?
[00:03:00] Alex: yes SSO/SAML for console, RBAC, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private. we'll attach the security pack with SOC2/ISO docs and our KMS integration patterns.

[00:03:20] [00:03:23] Samir: quick note on latency: hosted API with our curated models gives you pretty low cold-start because we keep warm pools for common sizes. for dedicated you get reserved GPU pools which removes noisy-neighbor variability and gives predictable throughput. private (VPC) has more variability depending on customer infra and network path.
[00:03:44] Tom: can you quantify? p99 numbers?
[00:03:46] Samir: rough numbers off the top: for 1k context tokens on hosted with our optimized runtime you'll see p50 ~120ms per token stream start? sorry that phrasing is messy. For text-generation p50 latencies for short responses are often sub-200ms per token after streaming starts; but your end-to-end p95/p99 depends on batching, prefix cache hits, and sequence length. with dedicated configured for your profile you can tighten p99 substantially and get better throughput per dollar because of reserved capacity.
[00:04:20] Jordan: we've heard about batching hurting latency. how does Redwood handle batching vs per-request latency?
[00:04:25] Samir: we do continuous batching with configurable latency SLOs; small requests can be configured to avoid batching if you need strict low latency, but that increases cost. there's also automatic prefix/KV caching for common prompts, which can drastically reduce token compute for repeat queries.

[00:05:05] Maya: what's the quick path: we sign up, we get free credits, we 1) run quickstart and 2) run a benchmark with our prompts?
[00:05:10] Alex: exactly. typical flow: self-serve sign-up, you get free credits, integrate with SDK (we have node/python examples), call generate/chat endpoints, check tokens and latency. if you like results we can ramp to a small dedicated pool or set up a private VPC install if you need strict residency.
[00:05:25] Priya: on the private option, does Redwood ship a control plane or do we keep everything on-prem?
[00:05:30] Riley: for Private we offer a customer-managed network with a private control plane option; there is a package for on-prem where the control plane can be in customer network, and integrations for KMS. we can share the deployment guides.

[00:06:00] [00:06:05] Tom: any gotchas on GPU drivers or specific hardware? we run on GCP and AWS.
[00:06:09] Samir: we support major cloud GPUs and NVidia stacks; the private package includes supported driver lists. for Dedicated we provision the GPU fleet for you but on-prem you need to match the supported SKUs. we'll provide exact kernel and CUDA versions in the runbook.

[00:06:38] Maya: ok. what about model versions and rollouts? we need ability to pin versions and do canary.
[00:06:43] Alex: yep, you can pin model versions per route and do canary/A-B rollouts with automatic fallback. Console gives per-route metrics and tracing.

[00:07:05] Jordan: pricing is important. how do we compare hosted vs dedicated? rough numbers?
[00:07:10] Alex: hosted is usage-based (per-token pricing). Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly/annual commits; unit cost per token for high-volume is usually lower on Dedicated. We'll send a pricing deck with sample scenarios. For the pilot we often recommend starting hosted to validate prompts, then move to dedicated if you need predictable latency and lower unit costs.

[00:07:45] Priya: do you support customer audit logs and exports for compliance?
[00:07:50] Riley: yes, audit logs via the console and we can stream logs to your S3/GCS or to Splunk. for enterprise customers we support longer retention and more detailed logs.

[00:08:20] [00:08:25] Samir: i wanna zoom into time-to-first-token for your team since you care. if you use our node SDK and the sample app we provide, devs can get a token in under five minutes: sign up, copy sandbox key, run sample repo. for custom integration expect 1-2 dev days depending on auth and pipelines.
[00:08:45] Tom: do you provide client-side telemetry to see request size and token usage?
[00:08:50] Alex: yes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards are available. we also have SDK hooks and tracing for latency breakdowns.

[00:09:10] Maya: for the pilot we want to use our prompts and see p95/p99 and cost per query. can Redwood run a benchmark using our prompt set?
[00:09:16] Samir: yes, we'll run a benchmark with a small dedicated window or a hosted load test. we'll need your prompt set and typical traffic profile. we can run for a day to capture variance.

[00:09:40] Jordan: will running benchmarks require us to put data into Redwood? we want to avoid sending production PII.
[00:09:45] Riley: you can anonymize or use synthetic prompts; also we can run benchmarks in a VPC private environment if needed. we'll follow your security team's constraints.

[00:10:05] Priya: what's the escalation path if we find a security gap?
[00:10:08] Alex: CSM and our security team will own the remediation. we'll share a SOC2 pack and a security questionnaire. if anything critical is found we can route to engineering for deeper review.

[00:10:30] [00:10:34] Tom: about model catalog: do you host open models and Redwood-verified profiles?
[00:10:38] Samir: yes, we curate open models and publish performance profiles. you can also bring-your-own model in Dedicated or Private but bring-your-own requires compatible format and sometimes compilation.

[00:11:05] Maya: ok, our success criteria: 1) p95 under 600ms for typical queries, 2) cost per query below $0.02, 3) security sign-off. if those are met we consider production by Q3.
[00:11:18] Alex: noted. we'll aim to structure the pilot to measure exactly those metrics.

[00:11:35] Jordan: what about rate limits and quotas?
[00:11:38] Riley: hosted has per-key rate limits but you can request increases; Dedicated provides predictable throughput without per-key throttling.

[00:12:00] [00:12:05] Priya: a quick question on encryption in transit and at rest — do you support customer-managed keys?
[00:12:10] Alex: yes, for Private and enterprise Dedicated we support customer KMS integration; for hosted you can opt into CMKs for encryption at rest in some plans. we'll include docs.

[00:12:30] Tom: any examples of existing customers in regulated verticals?
[00:12:33] Riley: yes a few fintech and health customers; we can red-acted case studies in the security pack.

[00:12:55] [00:13:00] Samir: quick technical aside: caching strategy — we do prefix caching and KV cache for long-running sessions which reduces both latency and cost for repeat queries. It can be configured per-model or per-route.

[00:13:25] Maya: that could help a lot with our support-ticket summarization where many prompts share common prefixes.

[00:13:40] Jordan: fine. can you also give an idea of staff effort to migrate from hosted to dedicated later?
[00:13:45] Alex: usually minimal: the API surface is the same, so app code changes are small; main work is around capacity planning and secret/config management. our SEs help with the migration plan.

[00:14:10] Priya: will you send an NDA or do we need one before you share security docs?
[00:14:14] Riley: we can send the standard NDA if you prefer; some high-sensitivity docs require an NDA. we'll ask your legal contact.

[00:14:30] Maya: okay, next steps recap?
[00:14:33] Alex: i will: 1) send quickstart guide + sandbox credentials and sample repo, 2) send pricing deck and example scenarios, 3) attach security pack (SOC2, KMS notes, deployment guides), 4) Samir will schedule a technical deep dive and benchmark run, 5) you share prompt set and SLOs.

[00:14:55] Jordan: sounds good. any blockers from our side?
[00:14:58] Maya: security will need to review the pack but otherwise we can start the quickstart this week.

[00:15:05] Tom: quick nit: does the quickstart include SDK for our current tech stack? we use python + node microservices.
[00:15:10] Alex: yes python and node samples; we'll include a small express sample.

[00:15:20] Priya: timeline again: we want pilot next month and decision by EoQ.
[00:15:25] Alex: understood. we'll aim for readiness.

[00:15:40] [00:16:00] Riley: i'll follow up with the security questionnaire contacts and next steps.

[00:16:05] Maya: thanks everyone.
[00:16:10] Alex: thanks all, we'll send the docs and get the follow-up scheduled.

[00:16:20] [END OF TRANSCRIPT - remainder of call was wrapping and scheduling follow-ups. Some cross talk and brief hold music at the end. Note: transcription may have minor errors on acronyms and timings.]
notes: Pilot plan: hosted quickstart then dedicated pilot
